title: Relative tensor and derived pullback on arbitrary ringed topoi
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] on small sites, where $A,B$ are sheaves of commutative rings and the structural ring map is $f^{-1}B\to A$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $E\in D(A)$ and $G\in D(B)$. Module pullback is $f^*M=A\otimes_{f^{-1}B}f^{-1}M$, using the sheaf tensor product and change of rings [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; its total left derived functor $Lf^*$ and derived tensor are computed using K-flat resolutions with flat terms, where K-flat means that tensor with every acyclic complex is acyclic. Exact inverse image is applied termwise to complexes. There is a canonical isomorphism in $D(A)$, natural in $E$ and $G$,
$$E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}Lf^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}E\otimes_{f^{-1}B}^{\mathbf L}f^{-1}G.$$
The right side retains the $A$-action from $E$; its underlying $f^{-1}B$-complex is the derived tensor of the scalar restriction of $E$ with $f^{-1}G$. The comparison is the derived balanced tensor associativity map, whose ordinary local formula is $e\otimes(a\otimes g)\mapsto ae\otimes g$, with inverse $e\otimes g\mapsto e\otimes(1\otimes g)$. No flatness of $A$ over $f^{-1}B$, boundedness, coherence, or finite Tor dimension is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08I6, lemma-variant-derived-pullback, full statement and proof, lines 3727-3760.

proof.text: Put $C=f^{-1}B$. Choose flat-term K-flat representatives $P$ of $E$ and $Q$ of $G$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Factor the ringed morphism through $(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),C)$, first with identity structural ring map and then with $C\to A$ on the identity topos. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], applied to the first morphism and to $f$, both $H=f^{-1}Q$ over $C$ and $f^*Q=A\otimes_C H$ over $A$ are K-flat with flat terms. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], $f^*Q$ represents $Lf^*G$ with its canonical resolution comparison. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] represents the left side by $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_A(A\otimes_C H))$.

source.place: Tag 08I6 (lemma-variant-derived-pullback), proof, expanded using Tags 06YS, 0G7E, 06YY and 06YU.

proof.text: The right side has the one-sided K-flat model $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_C H)$ with $A$ acting through $P$. To check its underlying $C$-derived object, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $R\to\operatorname{Res}_C P$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Since $H$ is K-flat, [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs] makes $\operatorname{Tot}(R\otimes_C H)\to\operatorname{Tot}((\operatorname{Res}_C P)\otimes_C H)$ a quasi-isomorphism. The source computes $(\operatorname{Res}_C E)\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}f^{-1}G$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. The target carries the displayed $A$-action. No claim that $\operatorname{Res}_C P$ is K-flat is used. Naturality and independence as an $A$-object are checked in Step 4.

source.place: Tag 08I6 (lemma-variant-derived-pullback), proof: definitions of the two derived tensors; Tags 06YP, 06YU for the one-sided computation.

proof.text: For every bidegree $(p,q)$ define $P^p\otimes_A(A\otimes_C H^q)\to P^p\otimes_C H^q$ by $p\otimes(a\otimes h)\mapsto ap\otimes h$, and its inverse by $p\otimes h\mapsto p\otimes(1\otimes h)$. The $A$- and $C$-balancing relations make both maps well-defined; their composites are identities since $p\otimes(a\otimes h)=ap\otimes(1\otimes h)$. Sections of $A\otimes_C H^q$ are not finite sums of $a\otimes h$, so define the forward map in two stages: $(p,\sum a_i\otimes h_i)\mapsto\sum a_ip\otimes h_i$ is an $A$-bilinear presheaf map $P^p\times(A\otimes_{p,C}H^q)\to P^p\otimes_C H^q$, and [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension] (with $\mathcal O=A$, $\mathcal F=P^p$, $\mathcal G=A\otimes_{p,C}H^q$) extends it uniquely to an $A$-bilinear map on $P^p\times(A\otimes_C H^q)$, which induces a map out of the sheafified tensor by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The inverse comes from the $C$-bilinear presheaf map $(p,h)\mapsto p\otimes(1\otimes h)$ by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. By the uniqueness in that extension lemma and in sheafification, maps out of either sheaf tensor are determined by their values on these local generators, so the two composites are identities. They are $A$-linear, with the target action on $P$. Take their direct sum over $p+q=n$. By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], both differentials send the generator to $a\,d_Pp\otimes h+(-1)^p ap\otimes d_Hh$ after this map. Hence they give an $A$-linear cochain isomorphism of the two models, without a flatness assumption on $C\to A$.

source.place: Tag 08I6 (lemma-variant-derived-pullback), ordinary tensor identity in its proof, totalized explicitly.

proof.text: The two cochain maps of Step 3 commute with maps of $P$ and $Q$: applying $u:P\to P'$ and $v:Q\to Q'$ on either side sends a generator to $a\,u(p)\otimes f^{-1}v(h)$. For a quasi-isomorphism in $P$, tensor with the K-flat complex $H$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs]; the resulting maps are $A$-linear, and quasi-isomorphisms of $A$-complexes are detected on underlying $C$-complexes since kernels and cokernels retain the same underlying abelian sheaves. For a quasi-isomorphism in $Q$, its image under $f^*$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]; tensor with K-flat $P$ preserves it by the same tensor lemma. Conjugating by Step 3 shows that the right-hand model also inverts this map, as an $A$-complex. The resolving-class equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], once for $A$ and once for $B$, therefore descends the natural cochain isomorphism along the product of these two equivalences to $D(A)\times D(B)$. Naturality squares persist for inverse quasi-isomorphisms and their composites, so this gives bifunctoriality on all derived morphisms and independence of both resolutions. Step 2 identifies its right endpoint with the required relative derived tensor, retaining the $A$-action just constructed. Its representative formula and inverse are precisely the balanced associativity formulas in the statement, so the descended comparison is the specified canonical map.
